outcome: ExHarness can accept new input, coalesce operation completions and recover/cancel safely while detached operations are in flight.
currentProblem: Detached tools introduce scheduling races: completion storms can trigger redundant model turns, user steering can race with model/tool work, and process failure can lose wakeups unless event ordering and recovery are explicit.
constraints: At most one model generation is active per agent invocation/session unless a future explicit concurrency contract is added.
Multiple operation updates may be coalesced, but no terminal result or user input may be lost or reordered across its declared causality boundary.
User steering and stop requests must preempt new dispatch and remain durable across restart where the runtime supports persistence.
Recovery must derive pending work from durable operation/effect state, not traces or model prose.
successCriteria: User input received while tools run is accepted and causes bounded next-turn behavior without waiting for unrelated long operations.
Near-simultaneous terminal updates are deterministically coalesced so they do not create an avoidable model-turn storm.
Kill/restart and stop/cancel probes preserve exact pending-operation identity, do not duplicate effects and converge to terminal/reconcilable state.
